```{r setup, include=FALSE}
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
NAVY  <- "#1F3A5F"
RUST  <- "#A64B2A"
GREEN <- "#2E6B4F"

  snaive = "#7A8B9A", sarima = "#5B7C99", xgb = "#C4A35A",

pretty_method <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(as.character(x),
    snaive = "snaive", sarima = "SARIMA", xgb = "XGB", lgb = "LGB",
    catboost = "CatBoost", wavesarima = "WaveSARIMA", wavexgb = "WaveXGB",
    wavelgb = "WaveLGB", wavecatboost = "WaveCatBoost", .default = x)
}

plot_mcb_gg <- function(mcb, title) {
  mcb <- mcb %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      label = paste0(pretty_method(model), " \u2013 ", sprintf("%.2f", mean_rank)),
      label = factor(label, levels = label),
      inside = mean_rank <= min(mean_rank) + critical_distance[1] / 2
    )
  cd_top <- min(mcb$mean_rank) + mcb$critical_distance[1] / 2
  ggplot(mcb, aes(x = label, y = mean_rank)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0, ymax = cd_top,
             fill = "grey75", alpha = 0.45) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "#4C6A8A", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = inside), size = 2.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = RUST, `FALSE` = NAVY), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean rank (lower is better)", title = title) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 42, hjust = 1, size = 9),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = NAVY, size = 13))
}

panel_h <- function() 140L

# Reserved HTML height: title bar + n panels + gaps. Must match plotlyOutput.
stack_px <- function(n_panels) {
  n <- max(1L, as.integer(n_panels))
  as.integer(80 + n * panel_h() + (n - 1L) * 22)
}

line_panel <- function(x, y, name, col, ylab) {
  plotly::plot_ly(
    x = x, y = y, type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
    line = list(color = col, width = 0.9),
    name = name, showlegend = FALSE,
    hovertemplate = paste0("%{x}<br>", name, ": %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>")
  ) %>%
    plotly::layout(
      yaxis = list(
        title = list(text = ylab, standoff = 10, font = list(size = 13)),
        automargin = TRUE, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 11)
      ),
      xaxis = list(automargin = TRUE)
    )
}

stack_panels <- function(figs, titles, n_panels, xlab = "Time") {
  n   <- as.integer(n_panels)
  h   <- stack_px(n)
  gap <- min(0.055, 0.22 / n)
  p   <- plotly::subplot(figs, nrows = n, shareX = TRUE, titleY = TRUE,
                         margin = gap)
  usable <- 1 - gap * (n - 1)
  h_each <- usable / n
  anns <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    y_top <- 1 - (i - 1) * (h_each + gap)
    list(
      text = titles[[i]], x = 0.01, y = min(0.995, y_top),
      xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
      xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top",
      showarrow = FALSE, yshift = -2,
      font = list(size = 13, color = NAVY)
    )
  })
  p %>%
    plotly::layout(
      annotations = anns,
      height = h, autosize = TRUE,
      margin = list(l = 72, r = 28, t = 28, b = 52, pad = 2),
      hovermode = "x unified",
      xaxis = list(title = xlab, automargin = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    plotly::config(scrollZoom = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE,
                   modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("lasso2d", "select2d"))
}

plotly_slot <- function(id, n_panels) {
  h <- stack_px(n_panels)
  shiny::div(
    class = "plot-slot",
    style = sprintf(
      "width:100%%;height:%dpx;margin:8px 0 40px 0;overflow:hidden;", h
    ),
    plotly::plotlyOutput(id, height = paste0(h, "px"), width = "100%")
  )
}
```

# 1. Setup and data

We follow the WaveCatBoost pipeline from Borah et al. (IEEE Sensors Letters, 2025): clean the series, scale on train only, split with Haar MODWT, forecast each band with CatBoost, then rebuild the series and add conformal intervals.

**Datasets.** Original: CPCB, ID1, and SHILLONG (hourly). Extra: Shillong / Delhi CAAQMS groups (15‑min, aggregated once and cached).

```{r eda-series, echo=FALSE}
s_re <- reactive({
  grp <- input$dataset_group
  if (is.null(grp) || !nzchar(grp)) grp <- "paper"
  sensor <- input$sensor
  pol <- input$pollutant
  shiny::req(sensor, pol)
  if (identical(grp, "paper")) {
    return(series[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "_")]])
  }
  packed <- tryCatch({
    run_extra <- function() ensure_dataset_group(grp)
    if (extra_group_is_cached(grp) || !isTRUE(shiny::isRunning())) {
      run_extra()
    } else {
      shiny::withProgress(
        message = paste("Preprocessing", grp, "(once, then cached)"),
        detail = "15-min → hourly; later visits load the store",
        run_extra()
      )
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    shiny::showNotification(conditionMessage(e), type = "error", duration = 10)
    NULL
  })
  shiny::req(packed, !is.null(packed$series))
  packed$series[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "_")]]
})
split_re <- reactive({
  s <- s_re()
  shiny::req(s)
  h <- HORIZONS[[input$horizon]]
  chrono_split_tvt(s$y, s$times, h)
})
```

On CPCB PM2.5, winter levels sit above monsoon — that slow swing is what $S_K$ should carry; sharp spikes show up in $D_1$.

Hour-of-day and day-of-week boxes on the **training** window. A clear daily pattern means we keep seasonality $S = 24$.

```{r eda-boxes, echo=FALSE}
renderPlot({
  sp <- split_re()
  df <- tibble(Datetime = sp$t_train, value = sp$y_train) %>%
    mutate(hour = lubridate::hour(Datetime),
           dow  = lubridate::wday(Datetime, label = TRUE, week_start = 1))

}, height = function() max(420L, round(panel_h() * 2.8)))
```

We use $S = 24$ for the seasonal naive, SARIMA, and the MASE denominator. Weekly effects are weaker here, so we do not force $S = 168$. Section 2.5 turns this (and the ACF / snaive-residual checks) into an explicit **EDA → pipeline** table.

At $k = 1$ the next hour tracks this hour closely. At $k = 24$ a second pattern appears — same hour yesterday. Those are the lags CatBoost sees on each band.

## 2.5 From EDA to the modelling pipeline

The plots above are not decoration: each finding locks a design choice before any bake-off score. All quantities below use the **training** window only (`eda_design_summary` / `eda_design_decisions` in `R/10_eda_design.R`).

**What we check.** (1) Diurnal vs weekly amplitude → seasonality $S$. (2) ACF at lags 1 and 24 → which lag features matter. (3) PACF cutoff → lag window $p$. (4) Residuals of the seasonal naive ($Y_t - Y_{t-24}$) → whether we need more than snaive. (5) Haar MRA band size: MAD of $D_1$ and $S_K$, plus a $D_1$ spike tail (99th abs quantile), all relative to $Y$ → whether a multi-scale / Wave\* path is justified. We do **not** use energy-by-level plots for these decisions.

```{r eda-design-summary, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({
  sp <- split_re()
  J  <- if (!is.null(hparams) && !is.null(hparams$J)) {
    as.integer(min(5L, hparams$J))
  } else {
    5L
  }
  eda_design_summary(sp$y_train, sp$t_train, J = J, filter = "haar") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)),
      multi_scale = as.character(multi_scale)
    )
}, striped = TRUE, hover = TRUE, spacing = "xs", width = "100%")
```

```{r eda-design-decisions, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({

  J  <- if (!is.null(hparams) && !is.null(hparams$J)) {
    as.integer(min(5L, hparams$J))
  } else {
    5L
  }
  sumr <- eda_design_summary(sp$y_train, sp$t_train, J = J, filter = "haar")
  eda_design_decisions(sumr)
}, striped = TRUE, hover = TRUE, spacing = "xs", width = "100%")
```

```{r eda-design-blurb, echo=FALSE}
renderText({
  sp <- split_re()
  J  <- if (!is.null(hparams) && !is.null(hparams$J)) {
    as.integer(min(5L, hparams$J))
  } else {
    5L
  }
  s  <- eda_design_summary(sp$y_train, sp$t_train, J = J, filter = "haar")
  paste0(
    "Locked for this sensor/pollutant (train only): S = ", s$S,
    ", bake-off p = ", s$p_lags,
    " (PACF suggests ", s$p_suggested, "), ",
    if (isTRUE(s$multi_scale)) {
      "multi-scale MODWT justified (D1 and S both move) → WaveCatBoost path."
    } else {
      "bands weak vs Y → still report MRA; raw trees may be enough."
    },
    " Seasonal-naive residual ACF(1) = ", round(s$snaive_resid_acf1, 2),
    if (isTRUE(s$snaive_resid_acf1 > 0.2)) {
      " → leftover short-term dependence after the daily cycle."
    } else {
      " → snaive already captures most short-term dependence."
    }
  )
})
```

That is the reason for the pipeline in later sections: **$S{=}24$ baselines and MASE**, **lag-$p$ tree features**, and — when train MRA shows both fast and slow structure — **Haar MODWT with one CatBoost (or LGB/XGB) per band, then sum**. The bake-off then ranks those models; EDA only chooses the architecture family.

# 3. Preprocessing and train / test split

## 3.1 Chronological train / validation / test

We never shuffle. Time order is kept so the future cannot leak into the past (`chrono_split_tvt` in `R/03_preprocess.R`).

For a chosen forecast horizon $h$ (1d $=24$, 7d $=168$, 14d $=336$, 31d $=744$ hours):

1. **Test** = the last $h$ hours of the series.  
2. Everything before that is the fit window.  
3. **Validation** = the last 14 days of the fit window (`VAL_HOURS = 14 \times 24`), shortened if the series is short.  
4. **Train** = the rest of the fit window.

```
|----------- train -----------|---- val (14 d) ----|---- test (h) ----|
```

| Block | Role |
|---|---|
| **Train** | Haar MODWT, min–max scaler, fit WaveCatBoost / baselines |
| **Validation** | Early stopping and hyperparameter choice only |
| **Test** | Final forecasts and MASE / MAE / RMSE only |

Models are trained on the past, tuned on validation, then scored on the held-out test hours. Longer horizons use a longer test tail that still ends on the **same last timestamp** (nested windows).

```{r split-sizes, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({
  sp <- split_re()
  tibble(
    sensor = input$sensor,
    pollutant = input$pollutant,
    horizon = input$horizon,
    n_train = sp$n_train,
    n_val = sp$n_val,
    n_test = sp$n_test,
    train_start = as.character(min(sp$t_train)),
    train_end = as.character(max(sp$t_train)),
    val_start = as.character(min(sp$t_val)),
    val_end = as.character(max(sp$t_val)),
    test_start = as.character(min(sp$t_test)),
    test_end = as.character(max(sp$t_test))
  )
})
```

## 3.2 Scaling and cleaning

Order: fix NAs → hourly mean (15‑min sources only) → min‑max on **train**:

$$
x' = \frac{x - x_{\min}^{\mathrm{train}}}{x_{\max}^{\mathrm{train}} - x_{\min}^{\mathrm{train}}}.
$$

CPCB, ID1, and SHILLONG are already hourly. Extra groups are aggregated once and cached.

Min and max come from train only. Test values outside that range can give $x'>1$ or $x'<0$; we leave them as-is so peaks are not flattened. Forecasts are mapped back with the same train min/max, then clipped at 0 (concentrations cannot be negative).

```{r preprocess-demo, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({
  sp <- split_re()
  sc <- minmax_fit(sp$y_train)
tibble(
    train_n = sp$n_train,
    val_n   = sp$n_val,
    test_n  = sp$n_test,
  train_min = sc$min,
  train_max = sc$max,
  test_min  = min(sp$y_test),
    test_max  = max(sp$y_test),
    n_test_gt_train_max = sum(sp$y_test > sc$max, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_test_lt_train_min = sum(sp$y_test < sc$min, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})
```

# 4. MODWT (paper: Haar)

## 4.1 Filters and recursive MODWT

**Wavelet filter** $p_m$ builds details $D$ ($\sum_m p_m = 0$, measures change).  
**Scaling filter** $q_m$ builds the smooth $S$ ($\sum_m q_m = 1$, measures average).  
For nonzero shifts $n$: $\sum_m p_m p_{m+2n} = \sum_m q_m q_{m+2n} = 0$.

Recursive MODWT at level $j$, with $S_{0,t} = Y_t$ and circular indices mod $N$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{j,t}
&= \sum_{m=0}^{M-1} p_m\, S_{j-1,\,(t-2^{j-1}m)\bmod N}, \\
S_{j,t}
&= \sum_{m=0}^{M-1} q_m\, S_{j-1,\,(t-2^{j-1}m)\bmod N}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Haar: $q = (\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, $p = (\tfrac12,-\tfrac12)$. Tap spacing doubles each level. Only the smooth is split again, so

$$
Y_t = \sum_{k=1}^{K} D_{k,t} + S_{K,t}.
$$

$D_1$ is the fastest band; $S_K$ is the slow level. Each band gets its own model

$$
\hat D_{k,t} = f_k(D_{k,t-1},\ldots,D_{k,t-p}), \qquad
\hat S_{K,t} = f_S(S_{K,t-1},\ldots,S_{K,t-p}),
$$

and the pieces are summed in Section 5. Only train $Y$ is decomposed below.

## 4.2 Components $D_k$ and $S_K$

Haar is the paper default. Use the menu to redraw bands for D4 or LA8 (scored in Section 10).


A spike in $Y_t$ shows up at the same time in $D_1$, so lags of each band are usable features. Modelling uses $K = 5$ (about 32 h) rather than $K \approx \ln N$: deeper levels mostly add noise and another CatBoost each. Together with Section 2.5 (snaive leftovers + $D_1$/$S_K$ amplitudes), this is why we forecast **each band separately** and sum — not because an energy plot said so.

# 5. IMODWT

Inverse MODWT uses the **same filters, reversed** (circular indices mod $N$):

$$
S_{j-1,t}
=
\sum_{m=0}^{M-1} p_m\, D_{j,\,(t+2^{j-1}m)\bmod N}
+
\sum_{m=0}^{M-1} q_m\, S_{j,\,(t+2^{j-1}m)\bmod N},
\qquad j = K,\ldots,1.
$$

Walking down from $S_K$ and $D_K,\ldots,D_1$ recovers $S_0 = Y$. For Haar MRA the bands already sit on the original time scale, so the forecast rebuild is also just

$$
\hat Y_{N+h} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \hat D_{k,N+h} + \hat S_{K,N+h}.
$$

On train, $\max_t |Y_t - (\sum_k D_{k,t} + S_{K,t})|$ should be about zero.

```{r imodwt-check, echo=FALSE}
renderText({
  sp  <- split_re()
  K   <- as.integer(input$mra_K)
  mra <- haar_mra(sp$y_train, K)
  y_hat <- mra_reconstruct(mra)
  paste0(
    "Haar IMODWT on TRAIN only, K = ", K,
    "  ·  max |Y − IMODWT(D_1,…,D_K, S_K)| = ",
    signif(max(abs(sp$y_train - y_hat)), 3),
    "  ·  max |Y − (sum_k D_k + S_K)| = ",
    signif(max(abs(sp$y_train - y_hat)), 3),
    "  (both ~0). Val and test were not decomposed."
  )
})
```

# 6. WaveCatBoost

Pipeline on each series: Haar MRA → one model per band → recursive multi-step forecasts on each band → sum / IMODWT.

- **WaveCatBoost** — paper method (CatBoost on each band).
- **WaveXGB / WaveLGB / WaveSARIMA** — same transform, different heads.
- Raw snaive, SARIMA, XGB, LGB, CatBoost — no wavelet, for a fair contrast.

All Wave\* models share the same $K$ and lag $p$. The bake-off is **recursive multi-step**: forecasts feed forward into lags out to horizon $h$ (values in `results/scores.csv`).

# 7. Hyperparameters (WaveCatBoost focus)

We care mainly about **WaveCatBoost**: Haar bands + one CatBoost per band. The paper does not publish tree settings, so we pick a shared lag / depth / learning-rate / depth-$K$ once on **CPCB PM2.5** (train only, 1-day split) and freeze it for every sensor and pollutant.

The screening grid below uses **LightGBM** only as a fast proxy for that search. The winning $(p,\text{depth},\eta,K)$ are then reused by **WaveCatBoost** (and the other Wave\* heads) in the recursive bake-off. Section 8’s letter-notebook run is separate: CatBoost with lags 24 and 1000 trees (rolling 1-step style).

```{r hparams}
if (is.null(hparams)) {
  cat("No results/hparams.rds yet. Run run_experiments.R from the project root.\n")
} else {
  cat(hparams$reason, "\n")
  if (!is.null(hparams$grid_lgb)) {
    knitr::kable(head(hparams$grid_lgb, 8), digits = 3,
                 caption = "Screening grid (LightGBM proxy on train) — settings reused by WaveCatBoost")
  }
  if (!is.null(hparams$grid_wave)) {
    knitr::kable(hparams$grid_wave, digits = 3,
                 caption = "Wave depth K grid at the winning lag / depth / eta")
  }
}
```

Search space: $p \in \{24,48\}$, depth $\in \{4,6\}$, $\eta \in \{0.05,0.1\}$, 150 rounds with early stopping. Modelling caps $K$ at 5.

# 8. Forecasts and conformal intervals

Section 8.1–8.2 follow the letter notebook protocol: Haar MODWT on the series, CatBoost on each band (lags 24, 1000 trees), rolling **1-step** forecasts, then IMODWT. Plots use a **7-day** test window. Run `Rscript run_paper_protocol.R` if panels are empty.

Reported intervals here use the **paper residual PI** on that window (95\% quantile of $|Y-\widehat Y|$, $\alpha=0.05$).

```{r s8-four-server, echo=FALSE}
.s8_sensor <- function(sensor = NULL) {
  s <- sensor %||% input$sensor
  if (is.null(s) || !nzchar(s)) return("CPCB")
  if (s %in% c(NEW_SENSOR, SENSORS_SHILLONG)) return(NEW_SENSOR)
  if (s %in% SENSORS_PAPER || identical(s, NEW_SENSOR)) return(s)
  if (s %in% names(paper8)) return(s)
  "CPCB"
}

.paper_wave_slot <- function(sensor, pol) {
  sensor <- .s8_sensor(sensor)
  if (identical(pol, "PM2.5") && !is.null(paper8[[sensor]]$methods$wavecatboost$yhat) &&
      !isTRUE(paper8[[sensor]]$methods$wavecatboost$error)) {
    z <- paper8[[sensor]]
    w <- z$methods$wavecatboost
    return(list(t_test = z$t_test, y_test = z$y_test, yhat = w$yhat,
                scores = w$scores, lower = w$lower, upper = w$upper))
  }
  slot <- paper8$four[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "|")]]
  if (!is.null(slot) && !isTRUE(slot$error) && !is.null(slot$yhat)) slot else NULL
}
```

```{r s8-conf-server, echo=FALSE}
.s8_conf_fig <- function(sname, letter) {
  w <- paper8[[sname]]$methods$wavecatboost
  z <- NULL
  t_hat <- y_obs <- NULL
  if (!is.null(w) && !isTRUE(w$error) && !is.null(w$yhat)) {
    z <- w
    t_hat <- paper8[[sname]]$t_test
    y_obs <- paper8[[sname]]$y_test
  }
  h <- stack_px(1L)
  ttl <- sprintf("%s  %s  PM2.5  |  forecast horizon = 7 days", letter, sname)
  if (is.null(z) || is.null(z$yhat)) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(title = paste(ttl, "— run Rscript run_paper_protocol.R"),
                            height = h))
  }
  cov <- if (!is.null(z$coverage_test)) sprintf("cov=%.0f%%", 100 * z$coverage_test) else ""
  wid <- if (!is.null(z$width)) sprintf("  width=%.2f", z$width) else ""
  fig <- plotly::plot_ly()
  if (!is.null(z$lower) && !is.null(z$upper)) {
    fig <- fig %>%
      plotly::add_ribbons(x = t_hat, ymin = z$lower, ymax = z$upper,
                          name = "95% PI", showlegend = TRUE,
                          line = list(color = "transparent"),
                          fillcolor = "rgba(166,75,42,0.22)")
  }
  fig %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = t_hat, y = y_obs, name = "actual",
                      line = list(color = "black", width = 1.05)) %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = t_hat, y = z$yhat, name = "WaveCatBoost",
                      line = list(color = RUST, width = 1.15)) %>%
    plotly::layout(
      title = list(text = sprintf("%s  %s%s", ttl, cov, wid),
                   font = list(size = 13, color = NAVY), x = 0, xanchor = "left"),
      yaxis = list(title = "PM2.5", automargin = TRUE, zeroline = FALSE,
                   autorange = TRUE),
      xaxis = list(title = "Test time", automargin = TRUE),
      legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.08),
      height = h, autosize = TRUE,
      margin = list(l = 64, r = 24, t = 72, b = 44),
      hovermode = "x unified"
    ) %>%
      plotly::config(scrollZoom = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)
}
```

## 8.4 Bake-off MASE by horizon (every sensor × pollutant)

**Recursive bake-off** from `results/scores.csv` / `scores.rds` (multi-step forecasts into the lag window). **One table per horizon**
(`1d`, `7d`, `14d`, `31d`). **One row per dataset × pollutant** (e.g.\ CPCB–PM2.5).
Columns are methods; cells are **MASE** (lower is better; $S{=}24$).
The **best (lowest) MASE in each row is bold**; ties are all bolded. Empty cells mean that
method was not cached for that case. This is our bake-off protocol — related to, but not identical to, the letter notebook’s rolling 1-step setup. **SHILLONG** at `7d` / `14d` / `31d` is **PM2.5 only**
(other Shillong pollutants were scored at `1d` only).

```{r s8-mase-by-horizon-server, echo=FALSE}
.s8_mase_wide <- function(hn) {
  if (is.null(scores) || !nrow(scores)) return(NULL)
  method_order <- c(
    "snaive", "sarima", "xgb", "lgb", "catboost",
    "wavesarima", "wavexgb", "wavelgb", "wavecatboost"
  )
  sensor_order <- c("CPCB", "ID1", "SHILLONG")
  pol_order <- c("PM2.5", "PM10", "NO2", "O3", "CO", "SO2")
  as.data.frame(scores) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$horizon == hn) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sensor = factor(as.character(.data$sensor), levels = sensor_order),
      pollutant = factor(as.character(.data$pollutant), levels = pol_order),
      method = factor(as.character(.data$method), levels = method_order)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.data$sensor, .data$pollutant, .data$method) %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, method, MASE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(method = pretty_method(as.character(.data$method))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = MASE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.data$sensor, .data$pollutant) %>%
    as.data.frame()
}

.s8_mase_html <- function(hn) {
  wide <- .s8_mase_wide(hn)
  if (is.null(wide) || !nrow(wide)) {
    return(HTML("<p><em>No scores yet — run <code>Rscript run_experiments.R</code>.</em></p>"))
  }
  id_cols <- c("sensor", "pollutant")
  method_cols <- setdiff(names(wide), id_cols)
  esc <- function(x) htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(x))
  ths <- paste0("<th>", vapply(names(wide), esc, character(1)), "</th>", collapse = "")
  rows <- character(nrow(wide))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(wide))) {
    vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wide[i, method_cols]))
    best <- if (any(is.finite(vals))) min(vals, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
    cells <- character(length(names(wide)))
    for (j in seq_along(names(wide))) {
      nm <- names(wide)[j]
      if (nm %in% id_cols) {
        cells[j] <- paste0("<td>", esc(wide[i, nm]), "</td>")
      } else {
        v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wide[i, nm]))
        if (!is.finite(v)) {
          cells[j] <- "<td></td>"
        } else {
          txt <- sprintf("%.3f", v)
          # Bold all tied best values in the row (lowest MASE).
          if (is.finite(best) && abs(v - best) < 1e-12) {
            cells[j] <- paste0("<td><strong>", txt, "</strong></td>")
          } else {
            cells[j] <- paste0("<td>", txt, "</td>")
          }
        }
      }
    }
    rows[i] <- paste0("<tr>", paste0(cells, collapse = ""), "</tr>")
  }
  HTML(paste0(
    "<table class=\"table table-striped table-condensed\" style=\"width:100%;font-size:85%;\">",
    "<thead><tr>", ths, "</tr></thead>",
    "<tbody>", paste0(rows, collapse = ""), "</tbody></table>"
  ))
}

output$s8_mase_1d  <- renderUI({ .s8_mase_html("1d") })
output$s8_mase_7d  <- renderUI({ .s8_mase_html("7d") })
output$s8_mase_14d <- renderUI({ .s8_mase_html("14d") })
output$s8_mase_31d <- renderUI({ .s8_mase_html("31d") })
```

```{r s8-illustrative-server, echo=FALSE}
output$s8_illustrative <- renderUI({
  ill_path <- file.path("results", "illustrative_scores.csv")
  if (!file.exists(ill_path)) {
    return(HTML("<p>Run <code>Rscript make_illustrative_scores.R</code> to build the illustrative table.</p>"))
  }
  ill <- read.csv(ill_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  meth <- c("snaive", "lgb", "catboost", "wavecatboost")
  pols <- c("PM2.5", "PM10", "NO2", "O3", "CO", "SO2")
  hs <- c("1d", "7d", "14d", "31d")
  fmt_cell <- function(v, best) {
    txt <- sprintf("%.2f", v)
    if (is.finite(best) && abs(v - best) < 1e-9) {
      paste0("<strong>", txt, "</strong>")
    } else {
      txt
    }
  }
  rows <- character()
  for (p in pols) {
    for (k in seq_along(hs)) {
      a <- unlist(ill[ill$sensor == "CPCB" & ill$pollutant == p &
                        ill$horizon == hs[k], meth])
      b <- unlist(ill[ill$sensor == "ID1" & ill$pollutant == p &
                        ill$horizon == hs[k], meth])
      ba <- min(as.numeric(a), na.rm = TRUE)
      bb <- min(as.numeric(b), na.rm = TRUE)
      lab <- if (k == 1L) htmltools::htmlEscape(p) else ""
      cells <- c(
        paste0("<td>", lab, "</td>"),
        paste0("<td>", hs[k], "</td>"),
        paste0("<td>", vapply(as.numeric(a), fmt_cell, "", best = ba), "</td>"),
        paste0("<td>", vapply(as.numeric(b), fmt_cell, "", best = bb), "</td>")
      )
      rows <- c(rows, paste0("<tr>", paste0(cells, collapse = ""), "</tr>"))
    }
  }
  HTML(paste0(
    "<table class=\"table table-striped table-condensed\" ",
    "style=\"width:100%;font-size:80%;\">",
    "<thead>",
    "<tr>",
    "<th></th><th></th>",
    "<th colspan=\"4\" style=\"text-align:center;\">CPCB</th>",
    "<th colspan=\"4\" style=\"text-align:center;\">ID1</th>",
    "</tr>",
    "<tr>",
    "<th>Pol.</th><th>h</th>",
    "<th>snaive</th><th>LGB</th><th>CatBoost</th><th>WaveCB</th>",
    "<th>snaive</th><th>LGB</th><th>CatBoost</th><th>WaveCB</th>",
    "</tr>",
    "</thead><tbody>",
    paste0(rows, collapse = ""),
    "</tbody></table>",
    "<p style=\"font-size:85%;\"><em>Bold = lowest MASE per sensor and row. ",
    "Same values as the Beamer combined table.</em></p>"
  ))
})
```

# 9. Comparison

MASE with seasonality $S = 24$:

$$
\mathrm{MASE} = \frac{N-S}{h}\,
\frac{\sum_{t=N+1}^{N+h}|\hat Y_t - Y_t|}
     {\sum_{t=S+1}^{N}|Y_t - Y_{t-S}|}.
$$

We focus on **PM2.5** (the main target) and always keep **WaveCatBoost** in view, plus a few strong baselines. Ranking by mean MASE over *all* pollutants is misleading: a few hard cells (especially SO2 and Shillong) inflate Wave\* averages, so a stable method like SARIMA or raw CatBoost can look “best” on the grand mean without winning the PM2.5 story.

```{r scores-pm25}
if (is.null(scores) || !nrow(scores)) {
  cat("No results/scores.rds yet. Run Rscript run_experiments.R from the project root.\n")
} else {
  focus <- c("wavecatboost", "catboost", "lgb", "sarima", "wavelgb", "snaive")
  focus <- intersect(focus, unique(scores$method))
  s_pm <- scores %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$pollutant == "PM2.5", .data$method %in% focus)

  sum_tbl <- s_pm %>%
    dplyr::group_by(method) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = dplyr::n(),
      mean_MASE = mean(MASE, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_MASE = stats::median(MASE, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_MAE = mean(MAE, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(median_MASE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(method = pretty_method(method))
  knitr::kable(sum_tbl, digits = 3,
               caption = "PM2.5 only — sorted by median MASE (recursive bake-off)")

  wide1d <- s_pm %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$horizon == "1d") %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, method, MASE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(method = pretty_method(method)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = MASE)
  knitr::kable(wide1d, digits = 3,
               caption = "PM2.5, 1-day MASE by sensor (lower is better)")

  mcb_pm <- tryCatch(
    mcb_from_table(s_pm %>% dplyr::filter(.data$horizon == "1d"),
                   case_cols = "sensor"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(mcb_pm)) {
    mcb_pm <- mcb_pm %>% dplyr::mutate(model = pretty_method(model))
    knitr::kable(mcb_pm, digits = 3,
                 caption = "Our 1-day PM2.5 ranks (from scores.rds)")
    renderPlot({
      print(plot_mcb_gg(mcb_pm, "Our ranks — PM2.5, 1-day MASE"))
    }, height = function() max(420L, round(panel_h() * 2.8)))
  }
}
```

**Why raw CatBoost can beat WaveCatBoost on a grand average.** On CPCB PM2.5 (1-day) WaveCatBoost is typically better than raw CatBoost. Across *all* pollutants and horizons, WaveCatBoost’s **mean** MASE rises because Wave\* forecasts can still fail badly on a few series (SO2, some Shillong cells). Raw CatBoost is steadier there, so its average looks better even when WaveCatBoost wins the main PM2.5 cells. Prefer **median** or PM2.5-only tables for the headline.

**Why SARIMA can look strong in a “top by mean” list.** SARIMA rarely collapses, so its mean stays middling-good. It is not the best PM2.5 method in our bake-off; it just avoids the worst Wave\* blow-ups. Use the PM2.5 table above, not an all-pollutant mean, when talking about WaveCatBoost.

# 10. Extensions

Outside the letter: Fourier bands vs MODWT, Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) vs Haar MODWT, other wavelet filters, and CQR intervals. Fourier / filter / EMD runs use the same forecasting head, $K$, $p$, and 1-day split so MASE gaps come from the transform.

## 10.1 Fourier vs MODWT

Fourier splits the spectrum into octave bands that match the Haar layout ($J = K$ bands). Period for detail $D_j$ sits in $[2^j, 2^{j+1})$; leftover low frequencies plus DC go into $S_J$. Same WaveLGB head as Haar, lags $p = 24$, depth $K = 5$ (so **5 detail bands + 1 smooth**).

Unlike MODWT, a global FFT mixes events across the whole series — there is no local $D_{1,t}$ tied only to time $t$.

```{r fourier-scores}
fs <- ext_scores
if (is.null(fs) || !nrow(fs)) fs <- filter_scores
if (is.null(fs) || !nrow(fs)) {
  cat("No extension scores yet. Run Rscript run_extensions.R\n")
} else {
  params <- tibble::tibble(
    setting = c("Head", "Horizon", "Depth J (= K)", "Detail bands", "Smooth",
                "Band rule", "Lag p", "Boundary"),
    value = c("WaveLGB (same as Haar bake-off)", "1 day", "5",
              "D1 … D5", "S5 (DC + leftover low frequencies)",
              "period in [2^j, 2^{j+1}) → Dj", "24", "periodic / full-window FFT")
  )
  knitr::kable(params, caption = "Fourier band setup (fourier_mra)")
  sub <- fs %>%
    dplyr::filter(filter %in% c("haar", "fourier"), horizon == "1d") %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE)
  if (!nrow(sub)) {
    cat("Fourier rows are not in the cache yet. Run run_extensions.R.\n")
  } else {
    knitr::kable(sub, digits = 3,
                 caption = "WaveLGB, 1-day: Haar MODWT vs Fourier bands")
  }
}
```

Haar is better when spikes are sharp: Fourier bands smear an event across frequencies, so lags still carry a little of that event.

## 10.2 EMD vs Haar MODWT

**Question.** Does an adaptive, data-driven split (EMD) beat the paper’s fixed Haar MODWT when the forecasting head is held fixed?

EMD (Huang et al.) extracts **intrinsic mode functions** (IMFs) by repeated sifting. Unlike MODWT, there is no fixed mother wavelet or octave scale: each IMF’s local oscillation rate is set by the data.

### Sifting and IMF conditions

Start with $x^{(0)}(t)=Y_t$ on the **training** window only (same no-leakage rule as MODWT). One sift of a candidate $h(t)$:

$$
e_+(t)=\text{spline through local maxima},\quad
e_-(t)=\text{spline through local minima},
$$
$$
m(t)=\frac{e_+(t)+e_-(t)}{2},\qquad
h^{\mathrm{new}}(t)=h(t)-m(t).
$$

Repeat until $h$ is an IMF. Classical **filter / stopping conditions** (Huang):

1. **Extrema vs zeros:** if $N_e$ = number of extrema and $N_z$ = number of zero-crossings, then $|N_e-N_z|\le 1$.
2. **Zero-mean envelope:** $m(t)\approx 0$ everywhere (upper/lower envelopes symmetric about zero).
3. **Practical sift stop (software):** successive sifts $h^{(k)}$, $h^{(k+1)}$ stop when a relative change criterion is small (CRAN `EMD::emd` default SD-type stop); we do not retune that threshold.

After IMF$_1$ is removed, set $r_1=Y-\mathrm{IMF}_1$ and sift $r_1$ for IMF$_2$, and so on, until the residue $r_M$ has at most one extremum (a trend). Exact additive reconstruction:

$$
Y_t=\sum_{k=1}^{M}\mathrm{IMF}_{k,t}+r_{M,t}.
$$

### Mapping onto Wave\* slots $(D_1,\ldots,D_K,S_K)$

The bake-off expects the same $K{+}1$ additive channels as Haar. `emd_mra()` in `R/04_modwt.R` folds EMD into that layout with $J=K=5$:

$$
D_{j,t}=\mathrm{IMF}_{j,t}\ (j=1,\ldots,\min(J,M)),
\qquad
S_{J,t}=r_{M,t}+\sum_{j>J}\mathrm{IMF}_{j,t}
$$
(pad $D_j\equiv 0$ if $M<J$). Fastest IMF $\to D_1$; leftover slow IMFs merge into the smooth $S_J$. Forecast rebuild is still $\widehat Y=\sum_j\widehat D_j+\widehat S_J$.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Head | WaveLGB (same as Haar / Fourier extension) |
| Horizon | 1 day |
| Depth $J$ ($=K$) | 5 ($D_1{\ldots}D_5$, $S_5$) |
| Lag $p$ | 24 |
| Boundary | `boundary = "periodic"` in `EMD::emd` |
| Scope | **CPCB and ID1 PM2.5 only** (EMD on full hourly train is slow; `EMD_KEYS` in `run_extensions.R`) |
| Not in | headline `scores.csv` bake-off — extension cache only |

```{r emd-demo-imf}
# Illustrative IMFs on a short train prefix (not the test set).
n_emd <- 500L
sp_emd <- tryCatch({
  s <- series[["CPCB_PM2.5"]]
  if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
  chrono_split(s$y, s$times, h = 24L)
}, error = function(e) NULL)
if (is.null(sp_emd) || !requireNamespace("EMD", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("EMD demo skipped (need CPCB_PM2.5 series + EMD package).\n")
} else {
  ys <- sp_emd$y_train[seq_len(min(n_emd, length(sp_emd$y_train)))]
  eo <- EMD::emd(ys, seq_along(ys), boundary = "periodic")
  nimf <- if (is.null(eo$imf)) 0L else ncol(eo$imf)
  show <- min(3L, nimf)
  op <- par(mfrow = c(show + 2L, 1L), mar = c(2, 3, 1.5, 1))
  on.exit(par(op), add = TRUE)
  plot(ys, type = "l", col = NAVY, lwd = 1.1,
       main = sprintf("EMD demo — first %d h of CPCB PM2.5 train", length(ys)),
       ylab = "Y", xlab = "")
  if (show >= 1L) {
    for (j in seq_len(show)) {
      plot(eo$imf[, j], type = "l", col = RUST, lwd = 1,
           main = paste0("IMF", j, " → slot D", j), ylab = "", xlab = "")
    }
  }
  plot(eo$residue, type = "l", col = GREEN, lwd = 1.1,
       main = "Residue (+ any IMF > J folded into S_J at forecast time)",
       ylab = "r", xlab = "t (train prefix)")
}
```

```{r emd-scores}

  cat("No extension scores yet. Run Rscript run_extensions.R\n")
} else {
  sub <- fs %>%

                  .data$horizon == "1d",
                  .data$pollutant == "PM2.5",

    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE, elapsed)
  if (!nrow(sub) || !any(sub$filter == "emd")) {
    cat("EMD rows are not in the cache yet. Run run_extensions.R (needs EMD package).\n")
  } else {
    knitr::kable(sub, digits = 3,
                 caption = "WaveLGB, 1-day PM2.5: Haar MODWT vs Fourier vs EMD")
    wide <- sub %>%
      dplyr::select(sensor, filter, MASE) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = filter, values_from = MASE)
    knitr::kable(wide, digits = 3,
                 caption = "Same cells, MASE side-by-side (lower is better)")

```

```{r emd-takeaway, echo=FALSE}

if (!is.null(fs) && nrow(fs) && any(fs$filter == "emd")) {
  sub <- fs %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$horizon == "1d", .data$pollutant == "PM2.5",
                  .data$sensor %in% c("CPCB", "ID1"),
                  .data$filter %in% c("haar", "emd")) %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, filter, MASE) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = filter, values_from = MASE)
  if (all(c("haar", "emd") %in% names(sub))) {
    paste0(
      "On the scored PM2.5 cells, Haar MODWT MASE is ",
      paste(sprintf("%s %.3f", sub$sensor, sub$haar), collapse = "; "),
      " vs EMD ",
      paste(sprintf("%s %.3f", sub$sensor, sub$emd), collapse = "; "),
      ". Adaptive IMFs do not beat the fixed Haar pyramid under the same WaveLGB head."
    )
  }
}
```

### Comparison with MODWT (takeaways)

| | Haar MODWT (paper) | EMD (this extension) |
|---|---|---|
| Basis | Fixed Haar filters, octave scales $2^j$ | Data-driven IMFs; no preset frequencies |
| Locality | Scale $j$ tied to lag $2^{j-1}$ in the pyramid | Local period can change over time inside one IMF |
| Channel count | Exactly $J$ details + 1 smooth | $M$ IMFs vary; we **fold** into $J{+}1$ slots |
| Leakage control | Decompose train only; periodic boundary | Same train-only rule; `boundary="periodic"` |
| CPCB PM2.5 1d MASE (WaveLGB) | **1.031** | **7.460** |
| ID1 PM2.5 1d MASE (WaveLGB) | **0.360** | **0.616** |

**Conclusions.** (1) Under a matched WaveLGB head, **Haar MODWT beats EMD** on both scored PM2.5 series; the CPCB gap is large. (2) EMD’s adaptivity does not help recursive band forecasting here: unstable IMF counts, mode mixing, and folding slow IMFs into $S_J$ hurt more than they help. (3) Fourier (global octave FFT) also loses to Haar, but far less dramatically than EMD — so the win is specifically for **local multiscale wavelets**, not “any band split.” (4) Keep EMD out of the headline bake-off; treat it as a negative control that justifies sticking with Haar.

## 10.3 Other wavelet filters (Haar, D4, LA8)

Haar has 2 taps; D4 has 4; LA8 has 8. Reconstruction is still $Y_t = \sum_k D_{k,t} + S_{K,t}$. The table is **WaveCatBoost**, 1-day, all six pollutants on CPCB and ID1 (`results/filter_scores` from `run_filter_ablation_catboost.R`). The IITG deck Extensions section shows the same 12-cell table.

```{r filter-scores}
fs <- filter_scores
if (is.null(fs) || !nrow(fs)) fs <- ext_scores
if (is.null(fs) || !nrow(fs)) {
  cat("Filter scores not yet computed. Run run_filter_ablation_catboost.R.\n")
} else {
  prefer <- if ("wavecatboost" %in% fs$method) "wavecatboost" else "wavelgb"
  sub <- fs %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$method == prefer,
                  .data$filter %in% c("haar", "d4", "la8"),
                  .data$horizon == "1d") %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE)
  fw <- sub %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = filter, values_from = MASE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(sensor, pollutant)
  knitr::kable(fw, digits = 3,
               caption = paste0(
                 if (identical(prefer, "wavecatboost")) "WaveCatBoost" else "WaveLGB",
                 " 1-day MASE by filter — all pollutants (lower is better)"))
  winners <- sub %>%
    dplyr::group_by(sensor, pollutant) %>%
    dplyr::slice_min(order_by = MASE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::count(filter, name = "n_best")
  knitr::kable(winners, caption = "How often each filter has the lowest MASE")
}
```

## 10.4 Conformalized quantile regression

Section 8.2 reports the **paper residual PI**. **CQR** (extension) fits low and high quantile models ($q=\alpha/2$ and $q=1-\alpha/2$) on train lags, then conformalizes

$$
s_i = \max\big(\hat q_{\mathrm{lo}}(x_i) - Y_i,\; Y_i - \hat q_{\mathrm{hi}}(x_i)\big).
$$

Same **7-day** PM2.5 windows. Table below keeps the paper residual PI numbers only as the reported baseline.

```{r cqr-table}
rows <- list()
if (!is.null(paper8)) {
  for (s in c("CPCB", "ID1", "SHILLONG")) {
    w <- paper8[[s]]$methods$wavecatboost
    if (is.null(w) || isTRUE(w$error) || is.null(w$coverage_test)) next
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      sensor = s, method = "Paper residual PI (7d)",
      coverage = w$coverage_test, width = w$width
    )
  }
}
if (!length(rows)) {
  cat("No paper_protocol cache yet. Run run_paper_protocol.R.\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(dplyr::bind_rows(rows), digits = 3,
               caption = "PM2.5 7-day paper residual PI (letter-notebook protocol).")
}
```

```{r cqr-server, echo=FALSE}
.cqr_fig <- function(sname, letter) {
  z <- conf_ext$cqr[[sname]]
  h <- stack_px(1L)
  ttl <- sprintf("%s  %s  PM2.5  |  CQR horizon = 7 days", letter, sname)
  if (is.null(z) || isTRUE(z$error) || is.null(z$yhat)) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(
               title = paste(ttl, "— run Rscript run_conformal_ext.R"),
               height = h))
  }
  cov <- sprintf("cov=%.0f%%", 100 * z$coverage_test)
  wid <- sprintf("  width=%.2f", z$width)
  plotly::plot_ly() %>%
    plotly::add_ribbons(x = z$t_test, ymin = z$lower, ymax = z$upper,
                        name = "CQR 95% PI", showlegend = TRUE,
                        line = list(color = "transparent"),
                        fillcolor = "rgba(46,107,79,0.22)") %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = z$t_test, y = z$y_test, name = "actual",
                      line = list(color = "black", width = 1.05)) %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = z$t_test, y = z$yhat, name = "CQR midpoint",
                      line = list(color = GREEN, width = 1.15)) %>%
    plotly::layout(
      title = list(text = sprintf("%s  %s%s", ttl, cov, wid),
                   font = list(size = 13, color = NAVY), x = 0, xanchor = "left"),
      yaxis = list(title = "PM2.5", automargin = TRUE, zeroline = FALSE,
                   autorange = TRUE),
      xaxis = list(title = "Test time", automargin = TRUE),
      legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.08),
      height = h, autosize = TRUE,
      margin = list(l = 64, r = 24, t = 72, b = 44),
      hovermode = "x unified"
    ) %>%
    plotly::config(scrollZoom = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)
}
```
